# Cheat sheets {#sec-cheatsheets}

These pages collect the commands, thresholds, and formulas you'll reach for most. Each table points back to the chapter that explains it.

## The GWAS pipeline at a glance

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
    G["Genotypes<br/>bed/bim/fam or pgen"] --> QC["QC<br/>missingness, HWE, MAF,<br/>heterozygosity, sex"]
    QC --> S["Structure<br/>LD pruning, kinship, PCA"]
    S --> N["SAIGE step 1<br/>null model + GRM"]
    N --> T["SAIGE step 2<br/>per-variant tests"]
    T --> P["Plots<br/>Manhattan, QQ, lambda"]
    P --> I["Interpretation<br/>clumping, annotation, eQTL"]
```

Chapters: @sec-qc, @sec-structure, @sec-gwas, @sec-saige, @sec-postgwas.

## Common QC thresholds

These are typical starting points, not laws. Record the values you used in your analysis plan (@sec-templates).

| Check | Typical threshold | PLINK flag | Chapter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Variant missingness | exclude if > 2% (strict) to 5% | `--geno 0.02` | @sec-qc |
| Sample missingness | exclude if > 2% to 5% | `--mind 0.02` | @sec-qc |
| Minor allele frequency | keep MAF ≥ 1% for common-variant GWAS | `--maf 0.01` | @sec-qc |
| Hardy–Weinberg | exclude if p < 1×10⁻⁶ (controls) | `--hwe 1e-6` | @sec-qc |
| Heterozygosity | exclude samples beyond ±3 SD of the mean | `--het` | @sec-qc |
| Sex check | F < 0.2 female, F > 0.8 male | `--check-sex` | @sec-qc |
| Relatedness | KING kinship > 0.0884 (second degree or closer) | `--king-cutoff 0.0884` | @sec-structure |
| Imputation quality | INFO / R² ≥ 0.3 to 0.8, depending on use | `--extract` on filtered list | @sec-qc |

## PLINK essentials

```bash
# Missingness and frequency reports
plink2 --bfile data --missing --freq --out qc/report

# Basic filters in one pass
plink2 --bfile data --geno 0.02 --mind 0.02 --maf 0.01 --hwe 1e-6 \
       --make-pgen --out qc/data_qc

# LD pruning, then PCA on the pruned set
plink2 --pfile qc/data_qc --indep-pairwise 200 50 0.2 --out qc/prune
plink2 --pfile qc/data_qc --extract qc/prune.prune.in --pca 10 --out qc/pca

# Remove second-degree relatives or closer
plink2 --pfile qc/data_qc --king-cutoff 0.0884 --out qc/unrelated

# Association with covariates (logistic for binary, linear for quantitative)
plink2 --pfile qc/data_qc --pheno pheno.txt --covar covar.txt \
       --covar-variance-standardize --glm hide-covar firth-fallback \
       --out results/gwas
```

## SAIGE essentials

| Step | Script | Key inputs | Key outputs |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 — null model | `step1_fitNULLGLMM.R` | PLINK file for GRM, phenotype file, covariates, `--traitType` | `.rda` model, `.varianceRatio.txt` |
| 2 — association | `step2_SPAtests.R` | Dosages (BGEN/VCF/PLINK), step 1 model and variance ratio | Per-variant results: `BETA`, `SE`, `p.value`, `AF_Allele2` |

## Reading effect sizes

| Quantity | Formula | Read it as |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Odds ratio | $OR = e^{\hat\beta}$ | Change in odds per copy of the effect allele |
| 95% CI | $e^{\hat\beta \pm 1.96 \cdot SE}$ | Range of plausible ORs |
| Z-score | $Z = \hat\beta / SE$ | Strength of evidence, signed |
| Two-sided p | $p = 2\,(1 - \Phi(\lvert Z \rvert))$ | Probability of a result this extreme under $H_0$ |
| Genomic inflation | $\lambda = \text{median}(\chi^2) / 0.4549$ | ≈ 1.0 is well controlled; polygenic traits in large samples run higher |

| β̂ | SE | p | OR | Conclusion |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0.25 | 0.05 | 6×10⁻⁷ | 1.28 | Moderate effect, strong evidence |
| 0.25 | 0.25 | 0.32 | 1.28 | Same estimate, too uncertain to conclude |
| −0.35 | 0.07 | 6×10⁻⁷ | 0.70 | Protective allele |

## Significance thresholds

| Threshold | Use |
| --- | --- |
| p < 5×10⁻⁸ | Genome-wide significance for common variants |
| p < 1×10⁻⁵ | "Suggestive", for follow-up only |
| 0.05 / number of genes (≈ 2.5×10⁻⁶) | Gene-based tests across ~20,000 genes |
| FDR q < 0.05 | Exploratory screens, PheWAS |

## HPC job scheduling: LSF and SLURM

| Task | LSF | SLURM |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Submit a script | `bsub < job.sh` | `sbatch job.sh` |
| Interactive session | `bsub -Is bash` | `srun --pty bash` |
| Request memory | `-M 16000 -R "rusage[mem=16000]"` | `--mem=16G` |
| Request cores | `-n 4` | `--cpus-per-task=4` |
| Name and logs | `-J name -o out.%J -e err.%J` | `--job-name=name -o out.%j -e err.%j` |
| Array job | `-J "chr[1-22]"`, index in `$LSB_JOBINDEX` | `--array=1-22`, index in `$SLURM_ARRAY_TASK_ID` |
| List my jobs | `bjobs` | `squeue -u $USER` |
| Job details | `bjobs -l <id>` | `scontrol show job <id>` |
| Cancel | `bkill <id>` | `scancel <id>` |
| Queues | `bqueues` | `sinfo` |
| Finished-job history | `bhist -l <id>` | `sacct -j <id>` |

Details in @sec-computing.

## Code comment tags

A small convention that keeps analysis scripts searchable:

```text
# TODO:  work still to do
# FIXME: known to be wrong; fix before using results
# NOTE:  why something is done this way
# XXX:   warning; read before changing
```

`grep -rn "FIXME" scripts/` before every release of results.
